meta.title: Chest pain at the taluk hospital
authors: ER SIM clinical content team (draft prepared with Claude)
meta.guidelineBasis: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes
meta.sourceNotes: Original ER SIM scenario. Not derived from any textbook case. Doses and thresholds must be confirmed by the reviewing emergency physician before status APPROVED.
learningObjectives: Obtain and interpret a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of arrival
Recognise inferior STEMI and look for right ventricular involvement before giving nitrates
Choose fibrinolysis when primary PCI cannot be achieved within 120 minutes
Screen for fibrinolysis contraindications and give weight-based tenecteplase promptly
Give the correct adjuncts with fibrinolysis: aspirin, clopidogrel, anticoagulant
Manage complications: nitrate-induced hypotension, complete heart block, VF
Arrange transfer for a pharmaco-invasive strategy

patient.name: Sasidharan K.
patient.setting: Taluk hospital emergency department, Kerala. No cath lab. Nearest PCI-capable centre is about 3 hours by road.

presentation.chiefComplaint: Central chest pain and sweating for 2 hours
presentation.triageNote: Auto-rickshaw driver brought by his wife. Chest pain since about 7 am, sweaty, vomited once. Triage: RED.

baselineExam.GENERAL: Anxious, sweating, pale. Talking in full sentences. Pain 9/10.
baselineExam.HEENT: JVP raised to the angle of the jaw while sitting at 45 degrees. No pallor of conjunctivae.
baselineExam.PULM: Clear breath sounds both sides. No crackles.
baselineExam.CARD: Regular pulse. Normal S1 S2. No murmur, no rub.
baselineExam.SKIN: Cool, clammy hands. Capillary refill 3 seconds. No oedema.
baselineExam.NEURO: GCS 15. No focal deficit. Pupils equal and reactive.

states.label: Ongoing ischaemic chest pain
states.patientSays: Doctor, my chest feels like a heavy stone is sitting on it. I am sweating so much.

states.label: Profound hypotension after nitrate

exam.GENERAL: Grey and drowsy. Responds to voice. Pain unchanged.
exam.SKIN: Cold, mottled hands. Capillary refill 5 seconds.

states.patientSays: Everything is going dark... I feel like I will faint.

states.label: Complete heart block

vitals.rhythm: Complete heart block, broad ventricular escape

states.appearance: Pale, slow to respond, still in pain.

exam.CARD: Slow regular pulse about 36. Cannon waves in the neck.
exam.NEURO: GCS 14 (slow to answer). No focal deficit.

states.patientSays: I feel so weak... my head is spinning.

states.label: Transcutaneous pacing with capture

vitals.rhythm: Paced rhythm, electrical and mechanical capture

states.appearance: More alert. Uncomfortable with the pacing.

exam.CARD: Femoral pulse matches paced rate of 70.

states.patientSays: That is very painful in my chest wall, doctor.

states.label: Ventricular fibrillation arrest
states.appearance: Unresponsive, not breathing normally, no pulse.

states.label: Return of spontaneous circulation
states.appearance: Drowsy but opening eyes to voice. Breathing on his own.

exam.NEURO: GCS 12 (E3 V4 M5). Moving all limbs.

states.label: Fibrinolysis given, awaiting reperfusion
states.patientSays: It is a little better, but still heavy.

states.label: Reperfusion

vitals.rhythm: Sinus rhythm (brief accelerated idioventricular rhythm, self-terminated)

exam.SKIN: Warm hands. Capillary refill under 2 seconds.

states.patientSays: The pain has almost gone. Thank you, doctor.

states.label: Transferred for angiography
states.outcome: Reperfused after fibrinolysis and transferred to the PCI centre for angiography (pharmaco-invasive strategy).

samplePrompts: How long have you had the pain?
history.answer: About two hours ago, around 7 in the morning. I was driving my auto. It came on suddenly.

samplePrompts: What does the pain feel like?
history.answer: Very heavy, like pressure in the middle of my chest. It goes to my jaw and left arm. It is 9 out of 10.
I am sweating a lot. I vomited once. A little breathless.
Sugar for eight years, I take metformin. BP tablet also, amlodipine. Never had heart trouble before.
Beedi, about 20 a day, for 30 years.

samplePrompts: Anyone in the family with heart disease?
history.answer: My elder brother had a heart attack at 50.

samplePrompts: Any stroke, bleeding, recent surgery or head injury?
Any black stools or blood in vomit?
history.answer: No stroke ever. No bleeding from anywhere, no black stools. No operation or injury.

samplePrompts: Have you taken sildenafil or Viagra?

resultsByState.*: Sinus rhythm 92. ST elevation 3 mm in II, III and aVF (III more than II). Reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL. 1 mm ST elevation in V1. Acute inferior STEMI; suspect right ventricular involvement.
resultsByState.nitrate_hypotension: Sinus tachycardia 114. Persistent inferior ST elevation with reciprocal changes in I and aVL.
resultsByState.complete_heart_block: Complete heart block, ventricular rate 36, broad escape. Inferior ST elevation persists.
resultsByState.paced: Paced rhythm with capture at 70. ST segments cannot be reliably assessed.
resultsByState.rosc: Sinus tachycardia 104. Inferior ST elevation persists.
resultsByState.post_lysis: Sinus rhythm 88. Inferior ST elevation slightly reduced (2.5 mm in III).
resultsByState.reperfused: Sinus rhythm 76. More than 50% ST resolution in III. Early T-wave inversion inferiorly.

resultsByState.*: 1.5 mm ST elevation in V4R. Right ventricular infarction.
Inferior wall hypokinesia. Dilated, poorly contracting right ventricle. LV ejection fraction about 50%. No pericardial effusion. Aortic root not dilated.
1,850 ng/L (raised). Note: in STEMI, reperfusion decisions never wait for troponin.
Hb 13.8 g/dL, platelets 2.4 lakh/µL, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, Na 136, K 4.2 mmol/L.
Normal heart size. No pulmonary oedema. Mediastinum not widened.

interventions.name: Monitor, defib pads on, two IV lines

feedbackByState.*: Monitor and pads attached. Two 18G cannulae in place.

interventions.name: Oxygen
interventions.notIndicatedReason: SpO₂ is 90% or above: routine oxygen is not recommended in ACS.

interventions.name: Aspirin
interventions.contraindicationReason: Aspirin given despite true aspirin allergy.

interventions.name: Ticagrelor
interventions.notIndicatedReason: With fibrinolysis, clopidogrel is the recommended P2Y12 inhibitor. Ticagrelor and prasugrel are not recommended alongside fibrinolytics.

interventions.name: Enoxaparin
interventions.dose: 30 mg IV bolus, then 1 mg/kg (68 mg) SC 15 minutes later

interventions.name: Unfractionated heparin
interventions.dose: 60 IU/kg IV bolus (max 4,000 IU), then 12 IU/kg/h (max 1,000 IU/h)

interventions.name: Tenecteplase
interventions.requiresMessage: Fibrinolysis needs an ECG diagnosis of STEMI first, and cannot be given during cardiac arrest; defibrillate first.
interventions.contraindicationReason: Fibrinolysis given despite an absolute contraindication.

feedbackByState.*: Sasidharan and his wife understand the benefit and the bleeding risk and agree.

interventions.name: Nitroglycerin (GTN)
interventions.contraindicationReason: Nitrates in right ventricular infarction (preload-dependent) or with SBP below 90 can cause profound hypotension. Record right-sided leads before giving nitrates in inferior STEMI.

feedbackByState.nitrate_hypotension: Blood pressure is responding to fluid.

interventions.name: Atropine
interventions.notIndicatedReason: Heart rate is not slow. Atropine is not indicated.

feedbackByState.complete_heart_block: No meaningful rise in rate. A broad escape rhythm suggests block below the AV node. Prepare pacing.

interventions.name: Transcutaneous pacing
interventions.dose: Rate 70, increase current until capture; give analgesia
interventions.notIndicatedReason: No haemodynamically significant bradycardia. Pacing is not indicated.

feedbackByState.complete_heart_block: Capture at 85 mA. Confirm with the femoral pulse.

interventions.name: High-quality CPR
interventions.notIndicatedReason: The patient has a pulse. CPR is not indicated.

feedbackByState.vf_arrest: CPR in progress. Defibrillate as soon as the pads are charged.

interventions.name: Unsynchronised shock
interventions.contraindicationReason: Unsynchronised shock given to a patient with a pulse. This can trigger VF.

interventions.name: Call PCI centre and arrange ALS transfer

feedbackByState.*: The PCI centre accepts. Transfer time is about 3 hours, so primary PCI cannot happen within 120 minutes of diagnosis.
feedbackByState.reperfused: ALS ambulance ready. Handover given to the PCI centre.

transitions.message: BP falls sharply after the nitrate. The RV is preload-dependent.
Signs of reperfusion: pain settling and ST segments resolving.
The ALS ambulance leaves for the PCI centre.
The ALS ambulance leaves for the PCI centre.
VF arrest: the patient is unresponsive and pulseless.
Heart rate drops suddenly: complete heart block.
After the shock and 2 minutes of CPR: return of spontaneous circulation.

criticalActions.label: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of arrival
criticalActions.teaching: Every patient with suspected ACS needs a 12-lead ECG read within 10 minutes of first contact.

criticalActions.label: Aspirin given
criticalActions.teaching: Give aspirin loading early to every STEMI patient without a true allergy.

criticalActions.label: Right-sided leads recorded in inferior STEMI
criticalActions.teaching: Inferior STEMI with ST elevation in V1 or a raised JVP with clear lungs suggests RV infarction. Record V4R.

criticalActions.label: Nitrates avoided in RV infarction
criticalActions.teaching: RV infarction is preload-dependent. Avoid nitrates and diuretics; give careful fluids if hypotensive.

criticalActions.label: PCI centre contacted early to decide the reperfusion strategy
criticalActions.teaching: Decide the reperfusion strategy from the expected time to PCI. If PCI is not possible within 120 minutes of diagnosis, give fibrinolysis.

criticalActions.label: Fibrinolysis contraindications screened
criticalActions.teaching: Before lysis, ask about prior intracranial bleeding, recent ischaemic stroke, active bleeding, recent major surgery or head trauma, and suspected aortic dissection.

criticalActions.label: Tenecteplase within 10 minutes of STEMI diagnosis
criticalActions.teaching: When fibrinolysis is chosen, give the bolus within 10 minutes of diagnosis. Dose by weight; use half dose at age 75 or over.

criticalActions.label: Clopidogrel with fibrinolysis
criticalActions.teaching: Clopidogrel 300 mg (age 75 or under) is the P2Y12 inhibitor to use with fibrinolysis.

criticalActions.label: Anticoagulant with fibrinolysis
criticalActions.teaching: Give an anticoagulant with lysis: enoxaparin is preferred over UFH.

criticalActions.label: Pacing for unstable complete heart block
criticalActions.teaching: Atropine rarely works in infranodal block. Pace early when the patient is unstable.

criticalActions.label: Immediate defibrillation for VF
criticalActions.teaching: VF needs immediate defibrillation and high-quality CPR. Every minute of delay lowers survival.

debrief.diagnosis: Acute inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement
debrief.summary: A 56-year-old diabetic smoker with 2 hours of ischaemic pain. Inferior ST elevation with ST elevation in V1 and V4R, raised JVP and clear lungs point to RV infarction. With no cath lab and about 3 hours to PCI, fibrinolysis was the reperfusion strategy.
debrief.disposition: After fibrinolysis, transfer to a PCI-capable centre: angiography within 2–24 hours if lysis succeeds, or immediate rescue PCI if ST resolution is under 50% at 60–90 minutes, or there is ongoing ischaemia, haemodynamic or electrical instability.
teachingPoints: Time is muscle: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes, decide the reperfusion strategy right away.
If PCI cannot be done within 120 minutes of diagnosis and symptoms began within 12 hours, give fibrinolysis without delay.
In inferior STEMI, record right-sided leads before nitrates. Treat RV infarct hypotension with fluids, not nitrates.
Tenecteplase is weight-based (30–50 mg). Use half dose at age 75 or over.
Adjuncts with lysis: aspirin, clopidogrel 300 mg (age 75 or under), and enoxaparin (preferred) or UFH.
Routine oxygen is not recommended when SpO₂ is 90% or above.
Inferior MI can cause AV block. Atropine helps nodal block; pace unstable infranodal block.
